extra.message: The JWT signing secret is hardcoded to the weak value 'aSecret' (jwt.secret=aSecret). JWTTokenUtil uses this value to sign and verify HS512 tokens for both admin and customer authentication. Anyone with the source/config can forge arbitrarily valid tokens, including tokens for administrator accounts, leading to full authentication bypass.

canTokenBeRefreshedWithGrace() ignores all validation and unconditionally returns true (line 150). AuthenticateUserApi (line 118) uses this method on the public /api/v1/auth/refresh endpoint, so an expired admin token (or one issued before a password reset) can be refreshed indefinitely, defeating token expiry and password-reset invalidation.

Product create/update/delete endpoints are mapped to '/auth/products' and '/auth/product/{id}' (POST line 103, PUT line 121, DELETE line 165, PATCH line 483). The /api/v*/auth/** security filter chain only requires ROLE_AUTH_CUSTOMER, and no method-level role check exists in this controller or the facade. Any ordinary authenticated customer can therefore create, modify and delete catalog products (privilege escalation / broken function-level authorization).

deleteImage() is exposed at '/private/product/image/{id}' and '/auth/product/images/{id}' (DELETE). It calls productImageService.getById(id) and deletes the image directly without verifying that the image's product belongs to the requesting merchant/store (unlike the sibling method at line 174). Any authenticated customer can delete any product image by ID (IDOR / broken object-level authorization).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Product image upload is mapped to '/auth/product/{id}/image' in addition to '/private/...'. Because /api/v*/auth/** only requires ROLE_AUTH_CUSTOMER, any authenticated customer can upload arbitrary image files to any product of the default store (the only check is that the product matches the resolved merchant store, not that the caller owns it). The uploaded original filename is later used to build server-side file paths, which can also enable path traversal/stored content depending on the configured CMS backend.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: deleteGroup() is mapped to DELETE '/api/v1/products/group/{code}' with no '/private' or '/auth' prefix and no authentication/authorization check in the controller or in productItemsFacade.deleteGroup(). No Spring Security filter chain matches this path (adapters only cover /private/** and /auth/**), so the endpoint is publicly reachable and any unauthenticated user can delete arbitrary product groups.

The cache-clear endpoint DELETE '/api/v1/auth/cache/store/{storeId}/clear' is protected only by the /api/v*/auth/** chain, which requires ROLE_AUTH_CUSTOMER, not an administrator role. Any authenticated customer can flush a store's configuration/content cache, causing a denial of service and forced cache reloads.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Product review update/delete are exposed under '/auth/products/{id}/reviews/{reviewid}'. The delete handler only verifies that the review's product id matches the path id (line 223) and never verifies the review belongs to the authenticated customer, so any authenticated customer can delete any other customer's review. The create handler (line 62+) likewise trusts the customerId supplied in the request body, allowing a customer to author reviews attributed to another customer.

extra.message: The authentication filter reflects the attacker-controlled 'Origin' request header directly into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any third-party website to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the /api/v1/auth and /api/v1/private endpoints and read the responses, exposing authenticated user data/actions. The same origin reflection without credentials appears in filter/CorsFilter.java:40.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The global exception handler returns the root cause message (rootCause.getMessage()) of arbitrary internal exceptions back to the API client (line 34-35, and similarly line 52-53). This leaks internal implementation details such as database/HQL errors, file system paths, and class names, aiding further attacks (improper error handling / information exposure).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: AES/CBC encryption uses a hardcoded, constant initialization vector (IV_P = "fedcba9876543210") for every encryption, and the AES key is defaulted to a hardcoded value (secretKey=7070200000000007 in the shopizer-core.properties profiles). Deterministic IVs and embedded keys make the ciphertext predictable and reversible, defeating the confidentiality of any data protected with this utility.
